steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's here.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (He led me here, and then covered his scent. Seems he's learned a handful of tricks from his time on land.)
Gladiia looks all around her.
She knows that someone once considered a friend is watching her closely.
But she does not hesitate, nor does she have the luxury to hesitate. She must retrieve the secrets of this ship as quickly as possible, and... return them to Ægir.
She wishes to return to her home. She wishes to offer it her aid, to avert calamity.
She looks at the key in her hands.
She swings open the door to the treasury.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Burning away all the nethersea brand is no small feat. I really ought to thank Kal'tsit and that jet-black creature of hers.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: The nethersea brand was unable to devour this reef. How unfortunate.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: Yet this is but one of myriad forms. You have not heard the prophecy, so you would not understand.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Prophecy? Do you think yourselves more than a band of refugees clinging to unknown lifeforms? What sort of future did you expect?

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: Our prophet is nothing like you. She never paints images of a false future, nor does she make promises she cannot fulfill.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: She spoke thusly: that countless massive scales shall merge into one and fly into the vast expanse. That the ocean will be smeared with light, forever growing, never drying up.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: That life and death will disappear and merge into a single entity. And at that time, even the false cosmos will be unable to eclipse the light of life.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: We shall all live in that ecosystem. We are all part of its magnificent Cycle. Life is born, is given purpose, seeks worth, and disappears. Only for the cycle to begin anew.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Sounds a whole lot like the sort of elaborate hallucination that can be cooked up by Originium Arts.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Is pushing Iberia to its current precipice, and slaughtering millions of lives, also part of your magnificent Cycle?

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: What do you possibly know?! Our kind does not consider the death of an individual to be an 'end.' Even when a life ends, it remains part of the Cycle!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You are angry, you are restless, and above all you are only human, heretic.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: ...You won't take me alive, Inquisitor. I know all about your heinous Originium Arts. We're all prepared to make the greater sacrifice.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: Our prophet will remain as out of reach to you as time itself slipping through your fingertips.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: High Inquisitor! Everyone in Gran Faro has long held a grudge against you people! The Penal Battalion cannot approach this place, and you are alone!

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: There's nowhere for you to run!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...Run?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Did you think we came here to entertain your sophistry about good and evil?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: He's not saying anything. This Iberian's a damn imbecile.

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: That black monster must have some kind of weakness. It's extremely durable, and can burn the nethersea brand with ease. What the hell is that thing?!

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: If you don't tell us, then by the time the Penal Battalion breaks free, we'll have already—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: —Lost?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Haha... You can't even handle Dr. Kal'tsit and the Inquisitor. Admit it, you've already lost.

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: Shut up!

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: I'm gonna make you— Wait, what are you doing?!

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: Why's your staff moving around?! What did you do?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Guess you spent so much time researching tentacle monsters that you forgot what Originium Arts are?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Seriously, get your head outta the clouds—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Guh—

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: You self-righteous bastard—! You think we haven't made ample preparations? Do you have any idea how long we've waited to flush out all of you scum colluding with the Inquisition?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't fall for his tricks. He's been hiding in this town for months now. Definitely a spy, and one well-versed in communications to boot.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: There's a chance our position has already been compromised.

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: Spies, spies! Of course the Inquisition's spies have been lurking among us since long ago!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I knew about you people because you never tried to hide it, and Amaia and I are close. But the Inquisition is different. They already don't like us, and if they wanted to hide...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: How would we ever know? After all, we've been nothing but laborers for generations.

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: Throw him out then, and feed him to our kin. The nethersea brand's growth is slowing down, and we need more nutrients to stop the Penal Battalion.

steps.name: Torturer Cultist
steps.text: We should also find an escape route.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Alright. I'll lead the way. Nobody's more familiar with this town than me, and we've left behind plenty of secret passages and underground depots.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You shouldn't be doing this, Thiago.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: How long have we known each other? And now you're gonna preach to me, you platitude-spewing zealot?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Stand up and walk. Time to become a part of the sea.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (I see.)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (A union of Originium and Ægir technology, a sturdier dome, the use of modules from nomadic cities on land, and the scalability of Originium Arts.)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (So this is how the genius of the Academy of Sciences viewed this land. And he managed to accomplish all this decades ago.)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (However...)
However, it's still not enough.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Ægir would be able to accomplish all this even without making contact with land. The integration of certain technologies cannot make the difference between victory and defeat.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I knew it... It's you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I wish it weren't, though, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Stay back. Take another step and I'll run you through, my old comrade-in-arms.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Skadi once thought herself the last of the Abyssal Hunters. Even she had thought you dead. Yet here you are.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: How insightful of you, Consul Gladiia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The circumstances don't seem to call for pomp and ceremony, Consul Ulpianus.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Feeling a bit nostalgic over titles long disused, are we?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We've known each other long enough. You should know very well what it means when a Hunter doesn't return.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've executed no fewer than you. And I can assure you that if any survivors have sunken into the abyss, I'd still hang them up to bake on the reefs before they ever got a chance to hear that song.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What about now? You reek of their scent. You've become one of them.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Don't lie to yourself, Gladiia. You are strict with others, but even more so with yourself.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Has wandering the land sufficiently satisfied your desire to torment yourself?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Hunter, I WILL kill you if your answer doesn't satisfy me.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia, most of this situation is largely out of your hands. I'm forced to approach the problem from a different angle.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What situation?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I... Like you, I have spent some time on land.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But what I saw was different. Did you come to understand the civilizations on land? No, you don't need to answer that, Gladiia the ever-arrogant.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: For their civilizations to survive, they tapped into Originium. It brought them opportunity and hope, but it also unprecedented calamity. To this day, they still have not fully analyzed its principles.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've witnessed many tragedies... They've given them the name 'Catastrophes.' They are foolish, ignorant, and weak, but the way they struggle and die is still harrowing.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And the Ægir... are no different.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You were never this sentimental in the past.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: No, sentiment has nothing to do with this.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: What I'm saying is, Ægir provoked the ocean in order to survive, and the ocean devoured it in return. Then, ocean gave birth to us.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We are products of a grotesque struggle. If we are unable to resolve this problem at its root, then we are unable to resolve it at all.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...What did you see, Ulpianus? What did you see to make you abandon the bonds of blood and the camaraderie we shared in battle?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: 'Sanctuary.' No doubt that is what those filthy cultists would've called it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Your familiarity with them only reduces my trust in you.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But the word is an apt description.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You know what Ægir once found in the depths of the ocean. Even if aren't a historian, a general education should've covered at least this.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Thousands of years ago, we reached the heart of the ocean. There, we found the point of origin. The cradle of civilization.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: As far as I know, Gladiia...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: He, and those Seaborn, in the deepest recesses of their nest...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I saw it. A 'construct.' No, not even the greatest science consuls of Ægir would have been able to make sense of what I saw.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I was unable to go deeper, as my injuries were too severe. My blood boiled, my ears rang, but still I felt—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: —The plurality of Him.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Well... That doesn't even slightly explain why you abandoned the team. You should have brought this information back.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: When millions of cries returned to a single point, the unhatched Seaborn all murmured the same name from within their differently-shaped sacs.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Or rather, Skadi.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Did it escape into the sea?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: No matter. It will return. And we'll continue to wait.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Ugh. Whoever decided that we were its 'kin'? Pathetic.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Mm. I see it too. The waves breaking unnaturally, like a twister. Or a mirage of an ocean city. What a strange sight.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Pah. It sure was lively today. Haven't had this much commotion since young Jamie and the chef died.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Nnh.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Pomegranate... flower.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Knight.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I wasn't expecting to see you back so soon. Did you come rushing to my ship because you missed the scent of your hometown? Have you gone completely mad yet?
The knight simply stares at Alfonso in silence.

But almost immediately, his sight fixates once again upon the ocean. Alfonso follows his gaze, and through the years in which time itself has become nebulous, day and night have already lost all meaning.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Are you still hunting the terrible waves?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I sure hope the blood of these monsters hasn't made you immortal. You can look forward to drowning one day. What a joyous thing.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Not a whole lot of wind today.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Waves, are the ocean's, breath.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: It still has not, stopped breathing.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: It has not, died.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Just like, the monsters, on land. They devour, destroy.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: The monsters on land.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Civilization!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Skadi.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I just remembered something else. How... did we manage to survive?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: How did YOU survive?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I can't remember the details. We hacked and we slashed, again and again without pause, until finally He...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Uh, what I meant was, if they really wanted us dead back then, would we have been able to survive?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Let me put it another way. Ægir doesn't know we're alive either.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They have no way of knowing.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Was it Swordfish who said she wanted to come to this ship?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes. She said this ship could bring us home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Mm, this does to be Ægir craftsmanship, though the shipwright, Breogan... The name doesn't ring a bell.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...You never did remember the scientists' names.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Do you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...It's such a relief, even talking to you like this.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Are you back for good, Laurentina? You won't leave us again, will you?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Haha, do you have to be so cheesy about it? I've also been with you, things just got a bit blurry in the middle there. Plus, it's kinda fun playing the part of a well-behaved nun.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Oh, but the captain had this outfit specially made for me by our friends over at Rhodes Island. She already knew my measurements even!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...To be honest, you grew a bit taller.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Wait, how do YOU know that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I... I was only helping out. The Captain said she didn't trust the tastes of the landwalkers.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Tastes? Ahaha...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We both know that's the last thing she cares about. Though, at least I can appreciate how she always makes sure these details are in place.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She said you like long dresses, and I did always have that impression. But... I rarely do these... tailoring activities.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ah, these symbols, they're Ægirian letters. We wrote them together.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They talk about you, about Gladiia, about me. About Ægir... our home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Whose idea was this? Couldn't have been mine, right?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We all came up with it together.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What about the style?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Swordfish picked it.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: How unlike her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We have to dedicate ourselves to battle.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Sure, sure, but no reason I can't doll myself up before the hunt, right?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Skadi, do you know what the first thought was, when I emerged from my stupor and remembered who I am?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It was to re-examine myself, to see how different I was from that clear, but distant, memory of myself on the other side of the shore.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Though I was dressed as a good little nun last time, I didn't particularly mind—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But now that my trusty companions have chosen my outfit for me, that makes me even happier. Can you understand how I feel?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm... Definitely better than when you woke up in a jar in Sal Viento.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Haha, that's for sure.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: So, that's why we're going to win over Mister Captain right now, yes?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Leave it to me.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No, impossible...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: When I sank into the trench along with the titan's corpse, enduring a pressure that no ordinary Ægir could bear, I saw something I'd never seen before.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia, you know why Ægir distances itself from the land. You know the many theorems as to why Originium and Catastrophes cannot invade us.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Most of them have been proven correct. The ocean is like a petri dish, nourishing and protecting the purity of Ægir.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But... what if the civilization we're so proud of is nothing more than mold growing on the back of some giant?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You were always exceptionally inquisitive, a quality that allowed you to make contributions in various fields, sowing the seeds for great breakthroughs. But to slander Ægir? You've changed so much I hardly recognize you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Plus, you should know the boundaries of what is appropriate. Your speculation about Skadi... You levy the cruelest of accusations against your fellow Hunter.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: 'Seaborn' is just a broad, catch-all name. As you know, their morphology is significantly more complex.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You've been concerned that Skadi might become an even higher form of them, have you not?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: First and foremost, I'm concerned that you've chosen the wrong path.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The 1st Company and the 4th Company perished along the way, one after the other, to create an opportunity for us to break through.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And you, the 2nd Company, stayed near the nest's entrance. It seems wrong to even describe it as a 'nest.' We'd entered a vast, singular entity, where we nothing more than tiny germs.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But germs are more than capable of killing a healthy person.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And we were successful, or so we led ourselves to believe.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I simply fell into a deep sleep, along with His corpse. Blood, if that luminous substance can even be called that, had drenched my whole body and enveloped me.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But I simply slumbered with His corpse for a long, long time. I hid in the crevasses of His empty shell, leaning against the remnants of His flesh, until all sounds around me fell silent.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But what about Skadi? It was she who dealt the final blow.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That was not a normal 'killing.' Nor was it a 'hunt.' It was 'feeding,' a feeding of their kind.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Your conjecture is both correct and faulty. Did you assume that all Hunters will eventually lose control and become Seaborn? No, not Skadi.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You already understand. Those who've witnessed Him, those of us who sank into the trench and floated back up, all understand.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You mean to say that...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: If anything goes wrong, we must kill her.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: She's YOUR Hunter.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You still haven't offered an explanation for your deliberate cover-up and betrayal. And you would have me trust your speculation like this?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'm not keen on your habit of staying silent. Maybe I'll have to take away your mobility and drag you back to Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: A pity that one of our consuls might finally fall in battle. Could harm morale.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Let's see you try.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia. How can you still claim to represent Ægir when you are so distraught about your own transformation?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is an opportunity. I don't expect your assistance, or even understanding, but some of us cannot afford to pass up this opportunity.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Only by uncovering the truth do we have a chance at survival.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And how is that related to what you're doing?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You came for the ship. I came for Breogan.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've already made a breakthrough. Breogan's evidence corroborates what I've seen. Truly an amazing man. To think he arrived at these same conclusions, in that era, under those conditions.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Those by your side— You already understand that only they are truly valuable. None of the land-dwellers will ever understand. And thus, he died in solitude.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I wouldn't say that nobody understands, but...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: 'But.' For someone as strong and resolute as yourself, how many times have you said 'but'?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We are colleagues. Together, we were the architects of this war. We should trust in each other more.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A final word of advice—don't return to Ægir. It is too soon, too dangerous. Too many things we haven't straightened out. Going back now is wasted effort, and you do not know what has become of it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Remain on land. Should something happen, of course—she IS my Hunter.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I will shoulder the responsibility.
Gladiia wants to say something else.

But when she turns her head, a tremendous cracking sound spreads through every corner of the room. A violent shuddering follows, and the truth filling the table is scattered across the ground, seeming to sear her vision.
'Leviathan.'

Before the chief designers of warfare proposed the Abyssal Hunter plan, before the Abyssal Hunters delved into their nest, Breogan chose a title that the foolish land-dwellers are obsessed with to this day.
He wanted to thoroughly elucidate the nature of calamities. He found the last piece of the puzzle on land.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: My... key... The smell of wheat... Homeland? My homeland supports me. My family supports me.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Until I, crush the ocean.
The two Hunters look at the brooding knight.
Gladiia clenches the key in her hand.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Then take a look at this monster. Take a good look. He appears human but is not human. Even the ocean's kin reject him.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Day in and day out, he searches for the terrible waves and seeks to quash them. An endless, futile pursuit.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Just like us.
